lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Hold there, traveller. Brackenfell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Greta at the Honeyed Hart keeps a bed for folk like you. Straight down this road to the square. It’s the tall house with the lantern.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: You lit the harvest fire. I never thought to see it burn again. You’re one of us now, whether you like it or not.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Road’s quiet. Just how I like it.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: The old watchtower, up the crag to the north-east. It held a beacon once. Burned out before my grandfather’s day. Children dare each other up there, though they swear to me they don’t.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Last village before the Greyspine passes. Sixty souls, one inn, one forge, and a chapel bell that no longer rings. Mind the river. The Stonewater is colder than she looks, and she doesn’t give back what she takes.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Well now, a new face! Hale sent you? Then you’re welcome under this roof. There’s a bed up the stairs, by the window. It’s yours while you stay. But I’ll ask a kindness in return. Osric at the mill owes me a sack of malt, and I can’t brew on promises. Fetch it for me?

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: You’re a treasure. Over the bridge east of the square, then follow the river downstream. You’ll hear the wheel before you see it.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The mill is over the bridge east of the square, then down the river. Osric will know what I’m owed.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: That’s the malt! Oh, bless you. There’ll be ale by week’s end. Here, for your trouble, and a bottle of the last batch.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: If you’ve a mind to stay useful: Brandt has been storming about since his hammer went missing, old Maren is short of frostcaps, and Brother Aldous frets over that silent bell of his. And the Elder likes company, out under the oak.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The whole village in my hall, and the fire lit in the square. I could weep. Sit, drink!

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: What can I get you, love?

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: It’s two gold, love, and your purse is light. Help a few folk around the village and come back.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Warm, and sweet with heather honey. The room feels friendlier already.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Three generations of Barleybrooks have kept this hearth. The beams came down from the beacon forest, and the recipe for the ale came from my gran, who took it from a traveller in trade for a night’s lodging. So you see, I’ve a soft spot for strangers.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Up the stairs at the back, the bed by the window. Sleep as late as you like.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Do me one small favour first and there’s a bed in it for you.

lines.speaker: osric
lines.text: Greta’s malt! I’d clean forgot, what with the wheel groaning all week. Here, take it, and tell her the next sack is on me. I’d carry it myself, but the stones won’t dress themselves.

lines.speaker: osric
lines.text: Mind the dust. A mill is no place for a naked flame, or a fool.

lines.speaker: osric
lines.text: The Stonewater turns my wheel, the wheel turns the stones, and the stones feed the valley. Simple as bread. Listen: you can hear her running true.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Unless you’ve come to tell me where my hammer is, I’ve work to do. My best cross-peen, gone from the bench three days back. And that boy Tobin can’t look me in the eye.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Hm. Start with the boy. He’s always underfoot in the square, when he should be at the bellows.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: That’s her! Where was she? The watchtower? I’ll tan his... no. No, I was a boy once, and that tower was a castle then too. Take this. I made it for no one in particular, and it seems that was you.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: She rings true again. Hear that? That’s the sound of a village with a working forge.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Find the boy. Tobin. Fair hair, guilty face.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: The watchtower, he said? Up the crag past the chapel. Mind your footing.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Iron from the Greyspine, charcoal from the pine, water from the Stonewater. Everything in this valley was made within sight of it. That’s rarer than you’d think.

lines.speaker: tobin
lines.text: The hammer? I, um. I only borrowed it! I was playing knights up at the old watchtower, and then it got dark, and I ran, and... I left it by the fire ring. Please don’t tell him it was me.

lines.speaker: tobin
lines.text: He wasn’t even cross! Well. He was a bit cross.

lines.speaker: tobin
lines.text: Bet you can’t beat me to the well!

lines.speaker: tobin
lines.text: A smith, like Brandt. I’m going to forge a sword as tall as Warden Hale. Taller!

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Hm. Young eyes. Good. The frost came early and my stores are thin. I need frostcaps: pale blue, and they glow a little at dusk. They grow where it is cold and quiet. By the lake, at the forest’s edge, near old stones. Bring me five.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Five, and not one bruised! You have gentle hands. Take this tonic. It will keep the mountain chill from your bones.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Sixty winters in this valley. I have buried more secrets in that garden than turnips.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Fevers, mostly. And grief, a little, though I don’t tell them that’s what’s in the tea.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The peace of the Dawn upon you. Forgive the quiet. Our bell rope rotted through at midsummer, and I have neither the coin nor the knees to replace it. A village without its bell is a body without a voice.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Would you? Marta keeps good hemp at her shop on the square. The Dawn remembers a kindness.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Hemp, and well laid! Give me one moment in the tower... there. It is done. Would you ring it? It ought to be a friend who rings it first.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Marta keeps good hemp rope at her shop on the square, east side.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The rope hangs under the tower, by the door. Pull, and let the valley hear.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Listen. The valley has its voice again.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: Only that the night ends. Every night, without fail. We find that worth a small stone house and a bell.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Quill’s Sundries. If I don’t have it, you don’t need it.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Thirty feet of the best. Don’t hang anything you can’t lift.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Baked this morning. Mostly.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: From Edda’s trees. Sweetest in the valley.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: I trade with the lowland caravans twice a year. The rest of the time I trade in gossip, and the price is always fair.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Brackenfell remembers its friends. Stay as long as you like. Stay for good, if the road will let you.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: The inn has its ale, the forge its hammer, Maren her remedies, and the bell its voice. Do you know how long it has been since Brackenfell was whole? We used to light a fire in the square at harvest’s end, and the whole valley would come. Light it tonight. You have earned the tinder.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Sit a while. An old man’s stories are all the entertainment this square can afford.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Before the bell there was the beacon on the crag, and before the beacon, only the stars. We have always found some way to say: here we are. Come and find us.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Begin with Greta at the inn. Everything in Brackenfell begins there.

lines.speaker: edda
lines.text: Wheat’s in, mostly. Chickens are out, always.

lines.speaker: edda
lines.text: Fairweather land, five generations. The soil is thin and the summers short, but the bread tastes of it. If you see Bram dawdling at the market, tell him the barn won’t sweep itself.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Shh. You’ll scare the char.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Mirrormere gives what she gives. She’s deep in the middle, mind. Deeper than the watchtower is tall, they say. Oh, and there’s one of Maren’s blue flowers on the shore yonder, if you’re collecting.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: A song for the traveller? I know nine. Seven of them are sad.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: This one’s called “The Road Goes Ever Up.” It isn’t about anything. The good ones never are.

lines.speaker: lark
lines.text: I came for one night, two winters ago. Greta’s ale is a kind of gravity.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: You walk loud.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Forest edge, north-west of the gate. Another on the rocks above the river, north of the bridge. And one past my cabin, where the ground stays cold. Don’t trample them.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: Hare. Grouse. Silence, mostly.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Have you seen a chicken? Not for any reason.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: My mum sells cloth and says I have to stay where she can see me. So I’m going to be a knight. Or a chicken farmer. I haven’t decided.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Patrol’s quiet. Keep to the roads after dark, friend.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Stonewater Bridge? Older than the village. Older than the chapel. Whoever built it meant for something to be on the other side.

lines.speaker: hilda
lines.text: Wool from the high pastures, dyed with Maren’s roots. Feel that. Go on.

lines.speaker: hilda
lines.text: It keeps us fed. And if my Pip offers to sell you a chicken, it isn’t hers.

lines.speaker: bram
lines.text: Apples! Cabbages! Oh. Sorry. Habit.

lines.speaker: bram
lines.text: Not a coin? Go on, then. Don’t tell Edda.

lines.speaker: bram
lines.text: Best in the valley. Only in the valley, mind, but still.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Safer than most. But there has been smoke in the pines north-west of the gate these three nights, and it is not Wren’s. Outlaws, come down off the passes before the snow. Hale cannot leave the gate, and I am too old to do more than worry. If you carry a blade and know its use, drive them off. Mind the big one.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: North-west of the gate, among the pines. You will see their rag on a pole before they see you, if you are careful. Eat before you go, and do not be too proud to run.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Then the children can pick berries at the wood’s edge again. This was my father’s, and it has hung on the wall long enough. Take it, with the village’s thanks.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Troubled me? They had my second-best tongs and a roll of files off the cart at the ford, a week gone. Their chief wears them on his belt like trophies. One ear, red beard. They camp west of the path up to the old watchtower. Bring my tools back and I’ll put a proper sword in your hand, not that kitchen iron.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Hah! Not a scratch on them. As promised: an arming sword, drawn out this spring and waiting for a hand. Keep the point low and your feet moving.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: There’s coin on the board for outlaws, and I’ll pay it myself. Five of them put down and the road is a road again. Two camps: one in the pines north-west of here, one under the old watchtower. Don’t take on more than you can see.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Five, by my count and yours. Paid in full. You’ve done the valley a turn, and I’ll not forget it.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Twenty-four, child. Frostcaps do not pick themselves.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Drink it when you bleed, not before. It is no use against foolishness.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Since you are the sort who walks: I have a tea I used to make from three herbs and my knees now refuse. Bogbean from the hermit’s pool, sunwort from the bee meadow, stonecrop from the old stones on the eastern hill. It is the only thing that lets Edda’s widow sleep.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: All three. And the stonecrop still wet. Sit, sit. I will brew it now, and you shall have the first cup.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Where did you… that is Corwin’s cap. Hob’s brother went down the old mine after silver, a good while back. So. It is the end of a long hope. Thank you for bringing it home rather than leaving it to the damp.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Corwin the miner. He went into the old workings north-west of here, up under the cliffs past the chapel, after silver; his brother Hob was the last to see him. The Warden barred the door afterwards. If you come across anything of his, I would be glad of it.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Finn pulled a man out of the lake at first light. He’s on a bier at the wharf, south end of the town. Go and look, if you’ve the stomach, before the gossips make a story of him.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text:
That’s Corwin’s hand. Alive, then, or he was. Let me see.

Bread. Fifty years of bread, in a cave on the shore. I barred that door and told myself it was to keep them out.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: That something went wrong below, before I wore this helmet. That Rowan went out to the shore every dawn and never said why. I didn’t ask. A man can keep a gate for thirty years that way.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Not here. Rowan knows the way to the lake cave; he’s walked it with a pail more mornings than I’ve slept. Go and ask him, and don’t let him tell you it’s nothing.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: Brass, and a number. OM fourteen: the Old Mine, Dunstan Pell. He dug under Corwin, a good while back.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: No. Dry as a bone inside and thin as a rake: he walked a long way on nothing, in the dark. That’s no lake’s work.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: The door in the north-west cliffs, up past the chapel. Hale barred it, but the Sexton kept the key, and old Sextons keep everything. Look in the crypt under the chapel.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: There’s a vestment chest in the sacristy that I’ve never had the heart to open. The Sexton’s things are in it. The crypt gate under the nave has a lock to match.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: First light, face down in the reeds. The lake gives drowned men back swollen. This one was thin as a rake and dry as kindling. Whatever he was, he walked to the water; he didn’t fall in.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: A man under a sheet! Hale said not to look. I looked. He’s got silver in his teeth.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: There’s a trunk up on the Hart’s roof walk. I climbed up. It’s locked, and Greta says it isn’t hers, but she looked cross.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: There’s lights behind the chapel after midnight. Two people. I’m not allowed out, so I didn’t see them.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Nothing. I’m being good today.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: You’ve one already, dear. Don’t be greedy with light.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Fill it before you go and mind the oil. Where you’re going, you’ll want it.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text:
Sit down, you’re making me tired. ... Hale has read it, then. I thought he might. I thought it would be me they came for one day.

The cave on the lake shore. The cellar of the Hart. I’ll tell you the rest, but not on my feet, and not today.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Tomorrow, I said. An old man needs a night to find the words. Sleep, and come back.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Hold there, traveller. No, sit, I am off the gate till morning. Brackenfell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Greta keeps a bed for folk like you. That is her, behind the bar.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Hold there, traveller. Brackenfell is a quiet place and I mean to keep it so. But you have the look of the road on you: tired, and honest enough. Greta at the Honeyed Hart keeps a bed for folk like you. It is the tall house with the lantern, on the square.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Good. That’s the end of it. This time.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: You haven’t the coin. Then it’s the cell. Come on.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: Paid. Keep your hands in your pockets in future.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: There’s no cell to hold you. Go on, then.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Eat it while it’s hot. I don’t do cold.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Three gold, love. Your purse says otherwise.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Four gold, love, and I’ll not haggle with a purse that light.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Up the stairs, the bed by the window. Sleep till you’re done.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: That’s a fine blade. Don’t draw it in my square.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Good. It sits well in your hand. My work.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Where did you get that? Those are my grandfather’s dies, fifty years back. Old Mine steel.

lines.speaker: maren
lines.text: You’re bleeding on my floor. Sit.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Off down a hole, love? I’ll keep the bed made.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Odd thing to carry. I’ll not ask.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: The Dawn keep you. You look as though you have seen the dead.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Still thinking about that man, aren’t you. So am I.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: A lantern by day. Either you’re lost, or you’re going somewhere I’d not.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Three weeks now without the bread. They will be counting.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: There is a stranger in town. Strangers ask about barred doors.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Then Hale is closer than I would like. Say nothing in the Hart.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: And if they go down?

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Then they find what Corwin found. Go, before the watch comes round.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The house on the south lane? Nobody’s lived there in years. Pass the salt, love, and don’t ask me twice.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Oh, that. I sell nothing to that house and I take nothing from it. Will you be wanting candles?

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Don’t look at the shutters. My father said never to look at the shutters.

lines.speaker: aldous
lines.text: There are houses the Dawn will not name, child. That is one. Leave it to her.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Sound work, that. Look after it and it will look after you.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Iron from the Greyspine, every piece. I don’t haggle.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Let’s see it, then.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: You’ve nothing I’d give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Not while the watch is asking after you. Square it with the Warden, then we’ll talk iron.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Not today, dear. Hale has been asking after you, and I’ll not buy from a name he is asking after.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Not while the watch is asking after you. I’ve a name to keep.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Let’s have a look, dear.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Whale oil. It stinks and it burns. Don’t spill it near the candles.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Grey silver, never stamped. Aye, I can. Three bars and ninety gold, and the edge will outlast the blade. Mind, I’ll want to know where you had it.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Done. Don’t draw it in the Hart.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: They say Tobin’s been up the Watch Bell more than the Watch has. A tin box, a lockpick, and a boy who will not say what he saw from the top.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: There’s a stone in the terrace wall below the Elder’s plaque with crooked mortar. Folk have stopped noticing it. The Magpie never did.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The Magpie keeps a cellar on Washing Lane, under a hatch no bigger than a cheese-board. Keeps the key somewhere sillier than a pocket.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The old Elder had a strongbox put in the quay when the Wharf was built. Reached from the water. I never knew a man who had the key.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The Magpie walks at dusk from the square to somewhere west of the weavers, same road each time. Nobody follows her. You’d have to be patient.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The shut house on the south lane. Don’t ask Marta. Don’t ask Finn. Ask nobody. Take a key, if you’ve one with a wren on it.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The mine door has been barred for fifty years. The Sexton kept the key, and old Sextons keep everything.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: My grandmother said the Old Mine’s foreman kept a strongbox below and wore the key round his neck. Nobody has been down to ask him.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: A drowned man on the wharf, dry as bone. The wise folk are keeping their windows shut.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Hale cries on the last day of the month. Pip told me. Pip tells everybody.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The Elder talks to the lake. Always has. Says it answers.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Nothing new, love. Same faces, same ale.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text:
The bread goes out at dawn. I carry it myself, and I am too old to be told it is a kindness.

The count stays kept. Sit. It will not hurt you to be counted.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text:
It is quiet. I did not know quiet could be this loud.

They are asleep. Thank you. I could not have said the names. I tried.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text:
Sit. You will want it from the start, and you will not like where it starts.

Fifty years back my father sold the last seam of the Old Mine to a Crown assayer, and the silver was singing, and he would not share it. He sealed the adit with twelve of his own shift still below. They did not die as you or I do. They stayed. They kept digging.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text:
It was never for their bellies. It was so that someone remembered them. Every dawn a loaf and a pail, left on the slab in the cave on the shore, and the count said aloud: one to twelve. As long as the count is kept they stay men. If it is not, the song takes what is left of the men in them, and they come up.

I carried it thirty years.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: I stopped it. Three weeks ago. Greta has found a buyer who pays double and wants the silver by the barrow, and I am old, and I thought: let it end with me. Pell walked out by the lake cave to ask why the bread had not come. You saw how far a man gets in daylight who has been so long under.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text:
Go the way Greta’s people ran the silver out. The Hart’s cellar has a wall that was never the end of the cellar: the fresh brick on the east side. A tunnel runs from there under the town to the lake cave.

The twelve stand by the slab. You will know what to do when you see them. I never did.

lines.speaker: rowan
lines.text: Go on. The Hart. The east cellar wall, newer brick than the rest. Take bread. Take a light. Take your courage in both hands, because it has been a long while since anyone went that way and meant well.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: I’ll not charge you for the stew this once, love. Don’t make it a habit.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The Hart’s never been so full. People want to be near other people, after.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: The count is kept and the gate is quiet. I’ll sleep tonight with the key out of my hand.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: I’ve left the old door unbarred. Nothing in it wants out now.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Silver for a blade? Aye, I’ll work it now. It’s only metal again.

lines.speaker: finn
lines.text: Nobody’s come out of the lake since. I check every morning.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: The cellar? Down the stair by the door, love, behind the rail. Take a candle, the steps are steep.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: If I look half asleep it is because I am. The bread is made while you are dreaming.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: Godwin Hobb. My mother baked at that oven and her mother before. Osric grinds it, I bake it, you eat it. That is a town.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: The Elder had six loaves off me every morning, paid by the month. Three weeks back he stopped. Never said why.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: You want it warm, find my Tilly at the stall by the bridge road. You want it warmer, be here before the light.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: Mind the rack.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: Fresh at first light. Not before, not after.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: The bell is back. Thirty years I have drawn the first batch on its stroke. These weeks I burned more than I sold.

lines.speaker: godwin
lines.text: I am awake all night, friend. That is the trade. You picked the one house in Brackenfell to creep into.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Come in out of the flour, or into it, there is no difference in this house.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: I am Avice. I married the baker for the warm kitchen and stayed for the same reason.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Greta takes two dozen rounds a day for the Hart and pays on the nail. If the whole town paid like Greta I would be a lady.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Osric was fretting about malt he owes the Hart. If you are walking to the mill you would do him a kindness to ask.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Mind the step, it is slick with flour.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Tilly! The stall!

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Hester Slate saw them carry him up. She said he weighed nothing. She has lifted enough to know.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Godwin! There is someone in the house! ... He is at the oven with a peel in his hand. I would go.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: Rounds, long loaves, and honey cake if Tamsin brought the honey. She did. So, honey cake.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: Tilly Hobb. I sell what my father bakes and I count better than he does.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: Giles Varrow walks the long way round to pass this stall. You can smell him coming. I do not mind it as much as I ought.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: The tinker down the row hears everything. If something is going on in this town, Diggory knew yesterday.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: Honey cake! Last ones!

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: Warm bread, warm bread.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: Father is himself again now the bell rings. Three weeks of burnt crusts, we had.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: I am calling my father, and he is holding something hot.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: Sit, if you are stopping. I am too old to look up at people.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: Idony Hobb. I have buried a husband, two hens I was fond of, and most of the people who knew me as a girl.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: Rowan was a boy with scabbed knees when they shut that hill. He has been an old man about it ever since.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: If you want to know what this town keeps under its tongue, ask who the bread was for. Not me. Ask Rowan.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: Mind my hens.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: Bell’s late. No. Bell’s not.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: So one of them walked out. I wondered who would live to see it. I did not want it to be me.

lines.speaker: idony
lines.text: At my age you are not frightening. You are only rude. Go home.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: Draw arm. Show me. Hm. You pull with your shoulder. Everyone does until someone tells them.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: Hugh Alder, fletcher. Shaft, feather and head, and I can tell you which goose the feather came from.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: Hale and I have shot at the butts every seventh day since we were lads. He is still the better shot and still pretends otherwise.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: Wren takes my broadheads by the dozen. Her cabin is west of the town; if you hunt, she is the one to ask.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: Straight grain. Always straight grain.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: Morning. How is the wind?

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: Hale asked me for two sheaves of arrows the day they found him. He has not ordered two in ten years.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: There are four hundred arrows in this house and I made every one. Leave by the door you came in.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Take a seat and a feather. If you are talking to me you can strip quills while you do it.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Gillian Alder. I keep the house, I bind the fletchings, and I keep Hugh from giving arrows away to friends.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Our Stephen has the cobbler’s shop and sleeps over it, alone, eating who knows what. It is forty paces. I count them.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Edda at Fairweather Farm saves me her goose feathers. It is east over the bridge, past the mill. Mind her geese.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Wipe your feet.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Is that Stephen? No.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Hugh says it is all finished now, one way or the other. Men say that. I have left the lamp trimmed.

lines.speaker: gillian
lines.text: Hugh. Hugh! Wake up, there is someone, and you have a bow on the wall.

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: A cask is thirty staves that hate each other, held by two hoops. That is all there is to know. It takes seven years to learn.

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: Laurence Byrd, cooper. The Hart’s ale, Goda’s beer, the salt fish: all in my oak.

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: My brother Randal builds boats on a lake with four boats on it. He had the hands to be a cooper.

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: Greta is waiting on malt from the mill before she can fill what I made her. Osric forgets. Somebody should jog him.

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: Tight as a drum.

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: Joyce! Hoops!

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: Greta wanted a cask moved in her cellar the week before they found him. Then she did not. I thought it odd then.

lines.speaker: laurence
lines.text: Joyce, the adze. No, the big one. Now, friend, which way is out? Show me.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: Come in. Mind the shavings. I would say I sweep them but nobody has ever caught up with a cooper.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: Felice Byrd. I shave hoops and keep the peace between a cooper and his daughter, which is the harder craft.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: Maren cured my hands when I could not hold a knife. People call her sour. I call her the reason I can work.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: Old Maren has more than tonics in that cottage. She read the dead man’s tally when nobody else could. If you find a thing you cannot read, there is your door.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: Mind the shavings.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: Lovely morning for it.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: I cried when I heard it. Silly. You do not know a thing holds your day together until it stops.

lines.speaker: felice
lines.text: Laurence! ... You have picked a house where everyone owns a blade with a handle at each end.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: That one is mine. Raised it, hooped it, tight first time. Father will tell you he helped.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: Joyce Byrd. I have done seven years at the block the same as any apprentice. I want "and Daughter" on the board.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: Old Wenn at the boatyard says a woman built the best boat that was ever on Mirrormere. He will not say who. I think it was his wife.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: The doors under the quay are the boat-houses, and Old Wenn has the keys. He will tell you a whole story before he tells you no.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: And Daughter. You will see.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: Tight first time.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: Everything in this town has changed but the sign over our door. I am working on that too.

lines.speaker: joyce
lines.text: I can swing a cooper’s adze all day. I can certainly swing it once.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: Feel that. No, with the back of your hand. That is Hilda’s weaving, and there is none better this side of the passes.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: Lindqvist. My grandfather carried cloth over the Greyspine on his back. I carry it across a counter and call it progress.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: Brandt Ironhand wears a shirt of my cloth that he has not paid Hilda for. I notice it every time he lifts his arm.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: If you want honest work, read the board at the Hart. If you want a good coat, come back with silver.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: Mind the bolts, they are not for leaning on.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: Good wool day. Dry.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: You will have heard. I sold the sailcloth they laid over him. I would rather not have known what for.

lines.speaker: anselm
lines.text: The shop is shut. Whatever you want will still be on the shelf in the morning, and so, I trust, will everything else.

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: Good day. Father will tell you the price is firm. It is not, but let him say it first.

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: I keep the counter and the book. Father keeps the opinions.

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: Lark has owed me a song for two winters. I have decided it will be about me and it will be flattering.

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: Brother Aldous was asking after rope for the bell. Marta Quill had hemp; the ropemaker is sore about it.

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: That blue is Wilmot’s. Look at it.

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: Lark! Two winters!

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: You are the one who got the bell ringing. I slept through the first one out of habit.

lines.speaker: sabina
lines.text: We are closed, and I am in my nightgown, and you are leaving.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: Hands. Let me see them. Hm. You work. Good, I do not sell to people who do not.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: Petronel Vey. I was a Lindqvist until I had the sense to marry out of drapery.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: That apothecary, Mossop. Jars of coloured water and a long word for each. Maren has forgotten more than he has read.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: Old Maren wants herbs gathered and her knees will not do it. Go and ask her. Say I sent you, she will be rude about it.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: Gloves would hide those.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: Fulk’s skins are late again.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: A drowned man with dry lungs. I have skinned enough beasts to know that is not drowning.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: I sleep with my shears. Think about that, and then think about the door.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: Stand straight a moment. No, I am not selling you anything, I only cannot help measuring.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: Jocelyn Lindqvist, tailor. My father sells the cloth and I cut it, and we argue about which is the harder.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: Bridget Malkin laughed at something I said on Tuesday. I have been trying to remember what it was ever since.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: I cut the coats for the Highfold wedding. If you go up that way, see whether Kester Wold has split the seams yet.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: That hem is a crime.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: Morning. Shoulders back.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: They asked me to stitch the shroud. I have made wedding coats this month. I did not like the change.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: Out. I will not be robbed in a house full of pins by someone who cannot see them.

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: Thorne. If it comes over the passes or goes out by them, a little of it stays with me.

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: I buy what Brackenfell makes and sell it where they have never smelled a tannery. Somebody must.

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: Hale would close the road for a fox. A warden who keeps everything out keeps trade out with it.

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: There is silver paid at the board for outlaws put down on the passes. I put some of that silver there myself.

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: Time is money. Mostly mine.

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: The passes, Hale! Think of the passes!

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: A dead stranger frightens caravans more than outlaws do. I want it explained, and I want it explained quietly.

lines.speaker: gilbert
lines.text: You are in a house with three locks and I heard every one. Sit down where I can see you while the watch is fetched.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: Salt by the block, pepper by the pinch, and no, the pepper is not cheaper for asking twice.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: Elinor Thorne. Gilbert has the warehouse and the temper. I have the stall and the customers.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: Master Sele lends me books and I return them unread with a remark. He has never caught me. Lettice has.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: The scribe keeps school in the mornings and every old paper in the town. If it was written down, Emmet Sele has it.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: Do not sneeze on the pepper.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: Fine salt, lake-dried.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: The town talks of nothing else. I sell salt. People will still want salt.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: Gilbert. Gilbert! There is a person. No, do not fetch the ledger, fetch the poker.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: Onions, oats, lamp oil, lard. Edda’s cabbages when Bram remembers to bring them.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: Simon Thorne. The other Thorne. The one with the shop and the debts, not the house and the opinions.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: My brother Gilbert owns the roof over this store, and reminds me on the first of every month.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: Hale wants lamp oil for the gate. There is a notice for it on the board, and the oil is at Marta’s, not mine, more’s the pity.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: Ned! Sacks!

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: Mind the lard.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: I had a customer ask for something to keep the dead out. I sold him garlic. It does no harm.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: There is nothing here worth a hanging. Oats. You would hang for oats?

lines.speaker: ned
lines.text: I am not allowed to talk to strangers. Are you a stranger? You look like one.

lines.speaker: ned
lines.text: Ned Thorne. I can carry a whole sack of oats. A small sack.

lines.speaker: ned
lines.text: Pip says she can climb the bell tower. She cannot. I cannot either, but I never said I could.

lines.speaker: ned
lines.text: There is a grey cat that sits on the rail of the hoist loft, behind the forge. If you are quiet it lets you.

lines.speaker: ned
lines.text: Race you! No? Fine.

lines.speaker: ned
lines.text: I was not running.

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: You get used to it. I did. Stand upwind, there, by the post.

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: Fulk Varrow. I turn hides into leather with bark, time and things you do not want named. Every boot in town began here.

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: Humphrey Slate sells the meat and I get the hide. He gets the customers and I get the smell. We are still friends.

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: Go along the lane where the washing hangs. People lose things there. People hide things there too.

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: Upwind, upwind.

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: Giles! The bark!

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: I know what water does to skin. I have a yard full of proof. That man had not been in the lake a day.

lines.speaker: fulk
lines.text: Nobody comes here by day. So you are either lost or desperate. Which?

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: I have washed. Twice. It does not come off, it only goes down a little.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: Giles Varrow. One day I will be the tanner. I am trying to think of anything else I might be instead.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: Tilly Hobb sells bread by the bridge road. I buy a loaf a day. We do not need a loaf a day.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: Brandt is always short a pair of arms at the forge. If I were not bound here I would be asking him myself.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: Does it show? The smell?

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: A loaf. Just the one.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: When the bell rang again I was at the pits. First thing in three weeks to sound better than this yard smells.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: Father! ... He sleeps like the dead. Lucky for you. Go on, go.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: Smell that. Leather and beeswax. That is what my brother’s stink becomes once somebody with skill gets hold of it.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: Tybalt Varrow, saddler. Harness, girths, the Elder’s chair. Winifred stitches finer than I do and I say so.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: The wheelwright across the lane makes the cart and I make what pulls it. Miles Ashdown and I have never had a bad word, which is rare between neighbours.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: Edda’s plough harness is due for mending. If you are going to Fairweather Farm, tell her it is ready.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: Saddle soap. That is all it wants.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: Good hide, that. Fulk’s.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: I made the straps for the bier. Hale wanted it done quiet. Nothing is quiet in a town of sixty.

lines.speaker: tybalt
lines.text: There is a child coming to this house in a month. I will not be gentle about who else comes into it.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Forgive me if I do not get up. I am stitching for two and sitting for two.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Winifred Varrow. I stitch the harness Tybalt cuts. Smaller hands, tighter seams.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Kat Ashdown leans on her gate at noon and I lean on mine, and between us nothing in Chapelgate goes unremarked.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Maren has a tea she makes me. She is always short of what goes in it. She would be glad of someone who can climb.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Kat! Have you heard?

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Not long now.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: I would like it all settled before the child comes. Tell me it is settled. Lie if you must.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Tybalt. Do not get up angry. Get up slowly, and angry.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: Pots, pans, kettles, and whatever you have heard, I heard it first. What will it be?

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: Diggory Pike. I mend what the smith is too proud to mend. A kettle is a small thing until it leaks.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: Goda Malkin says Greta waters the ale. Greta says Goda brews in a boot. I sell to both and agree with whoever is nearer.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: Somebody called the Magpie hides things about the town and leaves a note with each. I know three of the places. I will not say where. Look up, more often.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: Any pots to mend?

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: You did not hear it from me.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: A tally, silver in his teeth and a note for the Elder. I had all three before Hale had his helmet on.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: Alison, it is the one from the market! ... She says to tell you we have nothing but pans, and she has the heaviest.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: If he told you something, halve it. If he swore to it, halve it again.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: Alison Pike. He takes the stall and the talk. I do the mending that wants patience, here, in peace.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: Goda’s small beer would strip tin. I buy a jug every evening. Do not look at me like that.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: Greta at the Hart is always after someone to run an errand. She pays in coin and a bed.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: Halve it.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: Evening. Jug’s empty.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: Diggory has told that tale forty times and the man gets taller each time.

lines.speaker: alison
lines.text: I have a skillet in each hand. Diggory, light the lamp so I can see which one to use.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: Mind the spokes, they are only wedged. Give me a moment, I have a felloe half on.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: Miles Ashdown. Wheels, carts, barrows. If it rolls in Brackenfell I made it or I mended it.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: Brandt and I tyre the wheels together, him with the iron red and me with the water. Twenty years, and we have never cracked one.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: The mill is east over the bridge and down the river. Osric owes me for a cart wheel; mention it and watch him go deaf.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: Stand clear of the wheel.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: True as a die, that one.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: I built the handcart they brought him up on. Made it for turnips.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: I have a mallet that seats an oak spoke in one blow. Think it through.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: He is working. Talk to me, I know what it costs and when it will be done, which he does not.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: Kat Ashdown. He makes the wheels. I make them pay.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: Tamsin, Miles’s sister, lives two doors up with her bees. Twenty-seven, and writing letters to somebody. She will not say who.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: Tamsin’s honey goes to the Hart. If you want to know why it is called the Honeyed Hart, taste the ale.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: Winifred! Noon!
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: That will be two silver. Each.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: Well. Nobody will call this a dull year. I had been hoping for a dull year.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: Miles, there is a thief. A poor one. He has come to a house full of wheels.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: Walk slowly and do not wave. They are in a good temper today and I would like it to last.

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: Tamsin Ashdown. Eleven hives, and wax for the chandler. I prefer the bees to most company.

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: The hunter, Wren. She brings me heather from the high slope for the hives. I write to thank her. Often.

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: There is a bee meadow east of the chapel, off the crag path. Go quietly and they will not mind you.

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: Slowly. Slowly.

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: Heather’s out on the tops.

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: The bees were told. You have to tell them when someone dies or they leave. I did not know his name, so I said "a stranger".

lines.speaker: tamsin
lines.text: I keep bees, so I am not afraid of much. You have until I count to three, and I have already started.

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: Cord of ash, cord of oak. Ash for the forge, oak for the oven. What do you burn?

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: Jasper Holt. I keep the Hart, the forge and the bakehouse in fire. Without me this town is cold soup.

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: Wren knows the woods better than I do and never lets me forget it. She is usually right, which is the worst of it.

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: There is a lumber camp out on the forest road. A man called Hob worked it. He had a brother. Read the board at the old mine; do not ask me.

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: Ash or oak?

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: Dry wood! Seasoned!

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: I cut on every side of this town but one. North, under the cliffs, I leave standing. Now you know why.

lines.speaker: jasper
lines.text: I split logs for a living. You are standing in my house. Work it out.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: Mind the lines. If that sheet touches the ground I do it again, and I will know whose boot it was.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: Ysolt Pell. I married into the name. It came with a house, a father-in-law at the door, and a hill nobody mentions.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: Brandt took my Tobin at the forge when no one else would have a Pell. The boy loses his hammer and Brandt roars, but he feeds him.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: I wash for the Hart. Greta always knows who wants a pair of hands, ask her.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: Off the lines!

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: Dry by noon if the wind holds.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: They say he wore a brass tally. Do not tell Lambert what number was on it. Let me be the one.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: I have two boys and an old man asleep. Whatever you are after, it is not here, and I will scream the lane awake.

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: Have you seen a ewe with a torn ear? No. Nobody has. Warin will have my hide.

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: Davy Pell. I mind sheep for Warin Shaw. Ivo says the watch takes lads at sixteen. I am fifteen and three quarters.

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: My brother Tobin is at the forge. He borrows things. He does not mean it as stealing, he means it as knights.

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: There are outlaws camped up by the old tower, north of the chapel. Warin says they take lambs. I should like to see them try it with me there.

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: Torn ear. Left one.

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: Morning. Seen Warin?

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: Grandfather has not said a word since they brought the man up. He sits and he looks north.

lines.speaker: davy
lines.text: Mother! ... I am nearly in the watch. Stand where you are.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: You will be wanting something. People only talk to a Pell when they want something.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: Lambert Pell. I carried candles in the Old Mine when I was eleven. I came up one evening and Dunstan did not.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: Rowan stood beside me the day they barred the door. Fifty years. He has never once said my brother’s name to me.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: The mine is north-west, past the chapel and up under the cliffs. The Sexton kept the key. Ask the Brother what became of it.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: North. Always look north.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: Hm. A stranger.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: I went down to the wharf. They would not lift the cloth for me. I did not need them to. I know my brother’s hands.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: Fifty years I have slept by this door waiting for a knock. You are not the one I was waiting for. Get out.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: You have caught me in the town, which is rare. The flock is on the west pasture with the lad.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: Warin Shaw. Sheep, and a dog, and a house I use for sleeping. My niece married up to Highfold last month.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: Wren and I split the west slope between us. She takes what runs, I keep what grazes. We have never had a cross word.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: There are outlaws camped on the passes and a notice on the board that pays for them. I would do it myself for a ewe apiece.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: Away to me. No, not you.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: Rain by evening.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: I have pulled drowned sheep out of that lake. They are heavy. They say this one was light as a lamb.

lines.speaker: warin
lines.text: The dog heard you at the gate. I let you get this far to see what you would do. Now go.

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: Walk beside me if you want to talk. The rope does not stop for conversation.

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: Ulric Ferrin. Every rope in this town came off my walk. The well, the boats, the last bell rope, and the one before.

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: Brother Aldous sent to Marta Quill for his rope. Marta. A woman who sells buttons.

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: The well rope is new this spring, mine, and sound. If you want to see what a rope should be, go and look at it.

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: Mind the walk!

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: Keep it taut, keep it taut.

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: So the bell rings, on shop-bought hemp. Thirty feet. I would have laid forty and tarred the eye.

lines.speaker: ulric
lines.text: I have a hundred fathoms of cord in this house and I can tie anything. Do not make me show you.

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Do not touch the green ones, they are not fired. Everything else you may pick up, if you buy what you drop.

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Beatrix Ferrin. Ulric twists and I turn. Between us we make everything a house needs to hold and to hang.

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Old Maren and I have traded jars for salves since before Amice was born. Her tonic is why I can still close my hands.

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Maren’s stores are thin and her knees are bad. If you are a walker, she will send you for herbs and pay in tonic.

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Careful. Careful!

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Kiln’s hot today.

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Maren looked at him. She came here after and sat an hour by the kiln and did not say one word.

lines.speaker: beatrix
lines.text: Those shelves took me a month to fill. If one pot moves I will know it was you. Out.

lines.speaker: amice
lines.text: Father says I talk too much to turn the wheel evenly. Hello.

lines.speaker: amice
lines.text: Amice Ferrin. I turn the rope wheel and I am learning my letters from Master Sele.

lines.speaker: amice
lines.text: Lettice has read every book on the stall. Twice. She told me how one ends and I have not forgiven her.

lines.speaker: amice
lines.text: If you stand on the terrace by the Elder’s, there is a glass you can look through. You can see the whole market.

lines.speaker: amice
lines.text: One, two, turn. One, two, turn.

lines.speaker: amice
lines.text: I was not listening!

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: Those have a week left in them. I can tell by how you stand. Sit down, let me look.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: Stephen Alder. My father makes arrows; I wanted a trade where the customer comes back.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: Guardsman Ivo and I take a cup at the Hart most nights. He walks the wall and I mend what the wall does to his boots.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: The wall walk is open if you want to see the town from above. Stair by the north houses. Mind the gap by the tower.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: Heels, friend. Look to your heels.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: Evening, Ivo. Usual?

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: He had miner’s boots. Old pattern, pegged, not sewn. Nobody has made that boot here since my grandfather.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: I sleep over the shop for exactly this. That is an awl. It goes through ox hide.

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: One moment. Amice, that is a b, not a d. Now. How may a man of letters disappoint you?

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: Emmet Sele. I teach the children, write the letters, and keep the levy roll. I am the town’s memory and it treats me like its attic.

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: Brother Aldous says the Sexton’s papers lie under the chapel in a hand he cannot read. I can. He has only to cross the square.

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: The chapel has a crypt and the crypt has older books than mine. If you find the key, look at what the Sexton kept.

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: A b! A b!

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: Good day. Mind the ink.

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: A brass tally with OM on it. The mine kept its own roll, and it went under the chapel with the Sexton’s things. Nobody has asked me about it. Nobody ever asks.

lines.speaker: emmet
lines.text: If you have come for the levy silver, it is not kept here. If you have come for a book, I am almost flattered. Leave.

lines.speaker: lettice
lines.text: You may read standing up for as long as you like. If you sit down, you have to buy it.

lines.speaker: lettice
lines.text: Lettice. Master Sele took me in when the carts lost my father on the pass. I keep his stall and correct his sums.

lines.speaker: lettice
lines.text: Mistress Thorne brings her books back unread. She puts a ribbon at a different page each time. It is always a page with a picture.

lines.speaker: lettice
lines.text: There are notes and letters all over this town if you look. People here write down what they will not say.

lines.speaker: lettice
lines.text: That one ends sadly.

lines.speaker: lettice
lines.text: Do not bend it back!

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: Look, do not thumb the edge. The last man who tested my work that way is still learning to write with his left.

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: Roger Hask, cutler. Brandt makes the steel; I make it worth owning.

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: Brandt Ironhand is the best smith on this side of the Greyspine and his knives are doorstops. I say it to his face.

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: Brandt has lost his best hammer and half his temper. Find the one and you mend the other.

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: Edge like a razor. Mind it.

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: Father! Slower on the wheel!

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: Hale brought me the dead man’s knife to name the maker. No mark I know. Old iron, ground thin as a leaf.

lines.speaker: roger
lines.text: You walked into a cutler’s in the dark. Count your fingers on the way out.

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: Who is that? Come where the light is. No use, is it. Speak, then, I know a voice.

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: Odo Hask. Seventy-nine. I was a grown man when Rowan was a boy, and you may tell him I said so.

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: Idony Hobb and I are the last two who heard the hill when it sang. She will not talk of it. I will, if you ask me.

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: Look at the east wall of the Hart’s cellar. There is brick in it younger than I am. I never drank there after.

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: Who is that?

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: Good steel sings. Listen.

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: There. Hear it? I count my days by that bell. Three weeks I did not know if I was dead.

lines.speaker: odo
lines.text: I am blind, not deaf. Third board from the door. You are standing on it.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: Do not lean on her. She is green wood and steam and she is still deciding what shape to be.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: Randal Byrd. I build boats. My brother makes barrels, which are boats that gave up.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: Old Wenn taught me everything and still tells me I plank like a farmer. I would not trade him for a new shed.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: Finn Reedwater is at the end of the dock from first light. He found the man. He will tell it, if you ask kindly.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: Mind the strakes.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: Fair wind on the lake.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: They sent for me to look at the wharf. No boat brought that man. No keel mark, no oar. He walked out of the water.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: The tar pot is still warm. I would rather not waste it on you.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Twenty boats. There were twenty on this water when I had my hair. Now sit down, I am going to tell you about each one.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Wenn. Just Wenn. I built boats for sixty years and now I hold the keys and the opinions.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Randal is the best pupil I ever had and I will tell him so on my deathbed and not one hour before.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: The keys to the boat-houses are with me, and there they stay. Read the board on the wharf if you want to know how high the lake once stood.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Twenty boats!

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Planks like a farmer.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: I have seen what Mirrormere gives back. It gives back the drowned. That one, it did not want.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Eh? Is it morning? No. Then you are a thief, and I am too old to chase you. Shut the door on your way out.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Candles, cord, tar, tallow and lamp oil. Light and rope: there is nothing else a person truly needs.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Barnaby Crane, chandler. Tamsin’s wax, Ulric’s cord, my wicks.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Ursel says I should have asked the Elder which cave. Ursel says a good many things after the event.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The gate is short of lamp oil and there is a notice for it. Marta Quill has the flasks.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Tallow or wax?

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: Long evenings coming. Stock up.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: The Elder bought a dozen candles off me every month, "for the cave". I took it for a manner of speaking.

lines.speaker: barnaby
lines.text: I can lay my hand on a candle in the dark faster than you can find the door. Shall we see?

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: He will tell you light and rope are all a person needs. Ask him who cooks.

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: Ursel Crane. I keep the counter. I also ask the questions, since somebody must.

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: Mercy Garrick sweeps the widow’s step across the way, every week, a house nobody has lived in for years. Ask yourself why.

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: Widow Hale’s house is locked and has been since she died. Somebody has the key. It is not the Warden; I asked.

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: Which cave, though?

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: Mind the tar.

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: A dozen candles a month for a cave, and my husband never once said "which cave, Elder?" Thirty years I have been married to that.

lines.speaker: ursel
lines.text: Barnaby. Light a candle. We have enough of them. I want to see this person’s face.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Hm. ... Stone does not talk either. It is why I like it.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Garrow. Mason. Walls, hearths, and every stone in the churchyard since my father’s.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Finn and I drink at the same table at the Hart and say nothing. It suits us both.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: The north wall has a stair and a walk. I built the steps. From the top you can see the old tower on its crag.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Hm.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Good stone, that.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: The Brother has asked me for a headstone and given me no name to cut. I have left it blank. It will not be the first.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: I lift stone for a living. Go.

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: Mutton, pork when there is pork, and sausage you should not ask about. What will you have?

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: Humphrey Slate, butcher. Edda’s beasts, Warin’s sheep, my knife. Hester keeps the till so there is some left.

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: Hale has had three words with me about blood in the lane. Where does he think meat comes from? A tree?

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: The watch pays for outlaws put down on the passes. I would go myself, but who would cut the chops?

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: Fresh today! Mostly!

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: Do not ask about the sausage.

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: I helped carry him. I have carried sides of beef that were more alive. Dry, he was. Dry as jerky.

lines.speaker: humphrey
lines.text: Hester! Cleaver! ... No, I have it. Friend, I joint a hog in the time it takes you to reach that door.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: He shouts. He always shouts. The meat is good and the weights are honest, that is what matters.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: Hester Slate. I keep the block clean and the till closed.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: Avice Hobb and I were girls together. She married bread and I married meat, and we meet in the middle every market day.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: Ellen Marsh smokes fish down by the water. If you want lake trout, hers is the best.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: Honest weight, every time.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: Avice! A word!
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: I saw them bring him up the lane. I have told Avice and nobody else, and Avice has told the town.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: Humphrey has the cleaver. I have the other cleaver. There are always two.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: The bush is out, so the beer is ready. A farthing a jug and it will not put honey on your tongue or airs in your head.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Goda Malkin. I brew for people who work. Greta brews for people who sit.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Greta Barleybrook and I have not had a civil word in ten years and I would trust her with my last penny.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Osric at the mill owes half the town malt. If you are passing, tell him Goda remembers, and Greta is first in the line.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Bush is out!

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Farthing a jug.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Rings like it never stopped. I will say this for the Hart: Greta sent a cask round the night it came back, for everyone.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Bridget! The mash paddle! ... It is six feet of oak, stranger. I stir with it daily.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: Mother will tell you Greta’s ale is honey and airs. I drink at the Hart on Fridays. Do not tell her.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: Bridget Malkin. I do the brewing now, mostly. Mother does the selling and the feud.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: The tailor, Jocelyn. He measures me with his eyes every time I pass. I could do worse. I am checking whether I could do better.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: Lark plays at the Hart every evening. He says he knows nine songs and seven of them are sad. Ask him for one.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: Small beer, fresh.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: Friday. Do not tell her.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: People want beer when things change and beer when they do not. It is a steady trade, at least.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: Mother, do not get up, I have it. You. Out, before she finds the paddle.

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: Rush for seats, willow for carrying. Do not sit on the willow.

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: Adda. They call me the Rushworker. I cut my own reeds on the north shore and I have the hands to prove it.

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: My brother lives up by the fall, by himself. People say hermit and mean mad. He is neither. He is tired of people, which is sense.

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: Follow the stream up past the old tower and you come to a pool under a fall. If a man is there, let him be. He is my brother, and he is not mad.

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: Rushes, fresh cut.

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: Not on the willow!

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: A man comes out of the dark alone and they cover him with a sail. My brother went into the hills alone. I think of it.

lines.speaker: adda
lines.text: I weave by touch, so I do not need the lamp to find you. Out you go.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: The boat is not for hire today, the caulking is wet. And I do not go to the west shore, wet or dry.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Peter Marsh. I row what needs rowing. My father did, his father did. Marsh House has always had oars by the door.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Finn Reedwater is on that dock before I am up and after I am in. I do not know when the man sleeps.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: West shore, past the reeds, there is a cleft in the rock by the water. I have seen a light in it before dawn. I rowed the other way.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Penny across.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Not the west shore.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Finn found him. Everyone says so. Finn found him. That is right.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Ellen, take Will upstairs. ... I have an oar. I know it is a foolish thing to hold indoors. I am holding it.

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Mind the rack, it is hot. Trout and eel, done over alder. Here at the door, if you ask nicely.

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Ellen Marsh. He catches the fares, I catch the supper.

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Mercy Garrick mends our nets and will not take full price. Her brother is on the passes with the outlaws; she pays for him in knots.

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Peter knows every yard of the lake shore. Ask him about the west side and watch him find something to do with his hands.

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Smoked trout!

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Will! Off the dock!

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Peter came home grey that morning, before anyone had cried the news. He says he saw nothing. I have been married eleven years.

lines.speaker: ellen
lines.text: Peter. Wake up. Take the oar. Yes, the oar.

lines.speaker: will
lines.text: Finn says I am not to talk when the float is moving. Is the float moving? I am not allowed to look.

lines.speaker: will
lines.text: I am Will. I am eight. I can row if someone else holds one of the oars.

lines.speaker: will
lines.text: Finn caught a pike as long as me. He let me carry the tail end.

lines.speaker: will
lines.text: There is a dead man under a sail on the wharf. I am not allowed to look at that either.

lines.speaker: will
lines.text: Is it moving?

lines.speaker: will
lines.text: I did not touch it!

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: Talk if you like. I can mend and listen. I cannot mend and be looked at.

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: Mercy Garrick. Yes. That Garrick. He was a good boy and a bad man, and I knew him as both.

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: The widow Hale was kind to me when this whole lane was not. So I sweep her step. I do not need a better reason.

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: There is a notice at the Hart that pays for outlaws. I will not ask you not to. I will ask you to tell me, after, if one of them had one ear.

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: Mind the nets.

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: Knots hold. People do not.

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: The roads will be safer or they will not. Either way there is a man out there with one ear who is still my brother.

lines.speaker: mercy
lines.text: I leave a light in that window for someone and it is not you. Out.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: Good day. Humours out of balance, I can see it from here. A touch choleric. I have a tincture.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: Alaric Mossop, apothecary, late of the lowland towns. Two years here. They still call me the new man.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: Old Maren sells weeds in a twist of rag and half the town swears by her. I have glass jars. I have labels.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: The woman Maren sends people up the slopes for frostcaps and pays them in tonic. I call that hedge-craft. You may call it what you like.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: Choleric. Decidedly.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: I have a tincture for that.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: Dry lungs, they tell me, and the herb-woman is "reading" him. Reading. I offered a proper examination. I was not answered.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: I am a lodger here, I own nothing but books and bottles. Take a bottle. I will not tell you which ones are poison.

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: Do not shake my hand unless you want to be blue till Candlemas.

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: Wilmot Arden. Madder, weld and woad. Red, yellow and blue, and every colour you have seen in this town on a back.

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: Hilda weaves it and I colour it and Lindqvist sells it for three times what he gives the pair of us.

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: Hilda is at her loom by the river. She and the smith have a quarrel over cloth that neither of them will let lie.

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: Mind the blue!

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: Tom! Stir, do not splash!

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: Hilda came up that night and we sat by the vats till it was light. Neither of us wanted to be the one to say it.

lines.speaker: wilmot
lines.text: That vat has stood a week. It stains for life. Take one more step and I will tip you in.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: It does not wash off. I have tried. I have tried sand.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Tom Arden. I stir. Red on the first day of the week, blue for the rest of it.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: Tobin from the forge showed me the old tower. We were knights. He left something up there and now he is in trouble.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: You can get up on the Hart’s gallery by the outside stair. Nobody stops you. You can see who is at the well.

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: It does not wash off!

lines.speaker: tom
lines.text: I am stirring, I am stirring.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Reeve Wold. You are on Highfold ground now, and welcome, so long as the gates are shut behind you.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: I answer for Highfold to the Elder: the flock, the tally and the toll. Six houses and more sheep than Brackenfell has people.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Rowan has not climbed this hill in four years. I go down to him. That tells you how it stands between the two places.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: There is a toll ford on the west road, the far side of Brackenfell, when the guard is at his post. He has been at my son’s wedding for three weeks, in spirit.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Shut the gate behind you.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: Count them twice.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: We heard it up here a day late, as we hear everything. Brackenfell does its deciding and Highfold is told.

lines.speaker: jordan
lines.text: The Reeve’s door is never barred, by custom. It has never been needed. Do not be the reason I change it.

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: Come in and eat something. There is still wedding cake. There will be wedding cake at Candlemas.

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: Basilia Wold. I fed the whole hill for three days when Kester married, and I am still finding guests in the hay.

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: Rosalind is a town girl and thinks I do not see her looking down the valley of an evening. I looked the same way once.

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: If you are going down to Brackenfell, look for the stall with the blue cloth by the market cross. My cheese goes there, and it is not to be cut thin.

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: Have you eaten?

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: Whose trencher is this?

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: Down there they have their troubles. Up here I have forty borrowed trenchers to return and nobody will say whose are whose.

lines.speaker: basilia
lines.text: Another one sleeping it off? The hay is in the barn, the door is that way, and the wedding is over.

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: Married three weeks! Did you know? Everyone knows. I keep telling them anyway.

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: Kester Wold. The high flock is mine. So is the house, and so, God help her, is Rosalind.

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: Her uncle Warin keeps the low pasture. He looked me over like a ram at market before he would give her away.

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: The standing stones are north of us, a long walk up the valley. The flock will not graze near them. I do not ask the flock why.

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: Three weeks!

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: Come by, come by. Good dog.

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: Whatever they dug up or let out down there, it is a long way from my flock, and I have a wife to come home to.

lines.speaker: kester
lines.text: Ros, stay there. Friend, I have had three weeks of people walking into this house with gifts. You have no gift.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: You have come up from the town? Is the market on? Was Tilly at the stall? Tell me anything.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Rosalind Wold. Shaw, that was, a month ago. I can see the Hart’s roof from the top field if the air is clear.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: My uncle Warin will not come up to visit. Says the hill is all sheep. He keeps sheep. I do not understand men.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: If you go back down, tell Sabina at the draper’s the blue held in the wash. She will know what it means.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Is that the Hart’s smoke?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Morning! Any news from below?

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: I heard it. All the way up here, on the wind. I stood in the yard till it stopped.

lines.speaker: rosalind
lines.text: Kester. Kester! ... He will be a moment, he sleeps like a ewe. You should use the moment.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: Your Humphrey seen my Tilly’s face when the Varrow boy goes by?

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: Seen it? I have smelled why.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: avice
lines.text: He is a good lad under it.

lines.speaker: hester
lines.text: A long way under it.
lines.note: Aged 44; the block and the till.

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: Another letter went off with the carter. Sealed.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: To a man?

lines.speaker: kat
lines.text: She will not say. Which with Tamsin means it is worth knowing.
lines.note: Aged 40; keeps the yard and the accounts.

lines.speaker: winifred
lines.text: Give it till the heather is over.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: A loaf.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: You had a loaf yesterday.

lines.speaker: giles
lines.text: Father eats a great deal.

lines.speaker: tilly
lines.text: Fulk Varrow has not finished a loaf in his life. Take the honey cake and say what you came to say.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: The Warden has doubled the night watch. One man instead of half a one.

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: Gilbert says Hale would bar the road for a fox.

lines.speaker: diggory
lines.text: And what do you say?

lines.speaker: elinor
lines.text: That I should like to know what kind of fox.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: The boy lost your hammer again?

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: Borrowed it. He was a knight, I am told.

lines.speaker: miles
lines.text: You were worse at his age. You dropped an anvil in the lake.

lines.speaker: brandt
lines.text: That was never proved.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: What is in the green one?

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: A sovereign decoction for the vapours.

lines.speaker: petronel
lines.text: Mint. It is mint. Maren gives that away.

lines.speaker: alaric
lines.text: Hers is not in glass.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: You are pulling left.

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: The wind is pulling left.

lines.speaker: hugh
lines.text: How is young Ivo shaping?

lines.speaker: hale
lines.text: He can stand at a gate. Ask me again when something comes to it.

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: Has the miller sent your malt?

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Has he sent yours?

lines.speaker: goda
lines.text: He has not.

lines.speaker: greta
lines.text: Then for once, Goda Malkin, we are on the same side of something. Sit down, I will stand you a cup.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: Young Pell asked me the price of a guard’s boot.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Davy? He is fifteen.

lines.speaker: stephen
lines.text: Fifteen and three quarters, he says.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Tell him the boots are the easy part. It is the standing.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: Your mother looked at me today.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: She looks at everyone. She is deciding whether they drink at the Hart.

lines.speaker: jocelyn
lines.text: I am at the Hart now.

lines.speaker: bridget
lines.text: So am I. So we will both keep quiet about it.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: Come in, Father. It is getting cold.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: Fifty years I have sat here, and Rowan has walked past this door every one of them.

lines.speaker: ysolt
lines.text: He is an old man too.

lines.speaker: lambert
lines.text: Then he has not long to say it.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Is that Reedwater still out on the dock end?

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: Since first light.

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: A man who fishes that long is not after fish.

lines.speaker: randal
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: wenn
lines.text: Quiet. I built his father’s boat for the same reason.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Good. That’s the end of it. This time.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: You haven’t the coin. Then it’s the cell. Come on.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: Paid. Keep your hands in your pockets in future.

lines.speaker: ivo
lines.text: There’s no cell to hold you. Go on, then.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: You’ve nothing I’d give coin for. Outlaws carry better than they deserve, mind.
